transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Recording: auto
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Lee (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (ProsperPay Head of ML), Evan Cho (ProsperPay Infra), Priya Shah (ProsperPay PM)

Summary: Quick optimize walkthrough focused on batching, prefix vs KV cache, and cost model for conversation and retrieval workloads. Customer asked about latency SLOs, Dedicated capacity, and KMS/data residency.

Topics: batching strategies, KV cache sizing, prefix cache heuristics, cost per token models, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, pilot plan, security artifacts

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Aisha from Redwood, i'll kick off
Jonah and Marco from our SE team are here to walk through Optimize recommendations for batching and caching.
[00:18] Marta: thanks, yeah we are excited; we want to see how we can hit p95 latency targets while keeping token costs down for our payments chat assistant.
[00:28] Jonah: cool
quick agenda: 1) batching fundamentals and how it affects token cost, 2) prefix vs kv cache for context-heavy flows, 3) cost model with example numbers, 4) pilot/bench plan.
[00:38] Evan: quick q before we start
we're on GCP and use VPC peering for services, will that complicate the private deployment?
[00:45] Marco: good q
short answer: no, we support VPC peering and private deployments; we'll share the network diagram. for hosted you'll have TLS and tenant isolation, for private we'll do customer-managed network and KMS integration.
[01:02] Priya: want to call out our success criteria: p95 under 120ms for short chats (~200 tokens), and cost under roughly $0.003 per token on average.
[01:14] Aisha: got it
we'll use those as anchor numbers in the cost-model.
[01:22] Jonah: ok batching first
continuous batching inside the runtime groups requests into micro-batches to improve GPU utilization. the tradeoff is small added latency while reducing per-token compute cost. e.g., if you batch 8 requests vs single, throughput goes up, tokens/kg cost drops ~30-40% depending on sequence length.
[01:40] Jonah: important: adaptive batching
we tune batch sizes based on latency SLOs. for your p95 120ms target we'd cap batching window small, maybe 10-20ms, and rely more on prefix cache to reduce tokens.
[02:02] Marta: prefix cache? how is that different from KV cache? we've seen both terms in docs.
[02:08] Marco: good distinction: prefix cache stores the cached KV cache of transformer activations derived from a fixed prefix
it's super effective when user interactions reuse shared system prompts or static context. KV cache here we mean conversational long-context caching where you cache token key/value pairs for each user session to avoid re-encoding long histories.
[02:30] Jonah: in practice: prefix cache = cache common prefixes (system prompts, product descriptions) at model level; KV cache = per-session cached activations so you don't recompute earlier turns. both reduce tokens, but KV cache can blow memory if you have millions of active sessions.
[02:52] Evan: memory
that was our worry. we have ~200k monthly active users, peak concurrent chats ~3k. what's realistic for KV cache sizing?
[03:02] Jonah: yep
KV cache memory grows with sequence length and number of concurrent sessions. for e.g., 8k token history per session on a 7b quantized model might be ~40-50MB/session (rough number, depends on quant/FP). so for 3k concurrent it's large. that's where eviction policies and hot-session caching come in.
[03:24] Marta: so do you recommend KV or prefix for us?
[03:27] Marco: lean prefix cache first
most of your heavy tokens are reused system prompts and product templates. use prefix cache to cut repeated tokens; then selectively enable KV cache for high-value/enterprise sessions where latency matters most. this hybrid approach often gives 60-80% token reduction without huge memory cost.
[03:48] Priya: do you have concrete numbers we can use in our cost model?
[03:51] Jonah: yes
sample cost model we ran for a payments assistant: baseline (no cache, little batching): 1.0x token usage. With prefix cache alone: 0.55x tokens. With prefix + selective KV for 10% of sessions: 0.45x tokens. With aggressive batching (batch windows tuned) you can get further 0.38x effective token cost.
[04:18] Jonah: translating to dollars: if hosted cost baseline is $0.0065 per 1k tokens (example), after optimizations you're at $0.0025 - $0.0035 per token equivalent depending on mix
these align with your $0.003 target if we tune.
[04:36] Evan: those hosted numbers seem fine. what about Dedicated capacity pricing
we want reserved throughput and predictable latency.
[04:44] Aisha: Dedicated is ideal for steady throughput and strict SLOs; pricing depends on reserved GPUs and utilization. we'll send sample SKUs
generally Dedicated reduces unit cost at scale but has a commit. for pilot we recommend hosted + dedicated trial if volume justifies.
[05:02] Marta: security
we need SOC2, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. specifically, can we integrate with our HSM?
[05:12] Marco: yes
for Private deployments we support external KMS/HSM integration and full audit logs. we'll attach our security pack; Jonah will follow up with the architecture doc.
[05:22] Priya: one other question on model variants
if we fall back to smaller quantized models for cost, how do you measure hallucination/regression risk?
[05:30] Jonah: we run eval suites and quality regressions tied to prompt sets; Redwood Optimize flags regressions and has baseline comparisons. for pilot we'll run a sample eval with your prompts.
[05:42] Marta: can you show an example of latency vs batch size?
[05:45] Jonah: sure, pulling up slide
so this is approximate: single-shot average latency 60ms for short sequences; batch size 4 -> 85ms with 25% better throughput; batch 8 -> 120ms but double throughput. So if your p95 is 120ms we can push batching moderately but must keep windows small to avoid tail latency spikes.
[06:14] Evan: are these numbers per GPU or per endpoint?
[06:17] Jonah: per-request measured on our hosted endpoint simulating your traffic; single GPU benchmarks vary by model size. we'll share the raw benchmark sheet.
[06:24] Marco: also note kernel selection and quantization affect memory and speed
some models have optimized kernels that reduce KV memory footprint.
[06:34] [10:34] Speaker 1: (cross-talk / inaudible)
[06:52] Priya: what's the operational overhead of running prefix cache rules? do we need engineering effort to tag prompts?
[06:58] Jonah: you can auto-generate prefixes from common templates or mark them via API. Redwood Console shows hot prefixes and suggests which to cache. minimal effort for high ROI.
[07:12] Marta: perfect. for pilot we want to test two flows: 1) onboarding chat with lots of template text (prefix-heavy), 2) multi-turn payments troubleshooting (KV-heavy).
[07:24] Aisha: sounds good
proposed pilot: 2 weeks with staged ramp: week 1 run hosted with prefix cache + adaptive batching; week 2 enable KV for VIP sessions and compare. we'll measure p95, avg tokens/session, and cost.
[07:36] Evan: how do we instrument tokens and cost in the console? we need per-route breakdowns.
[07:42] Marco: Redwood Console has per-route token breakdown, latency histograms, and cost attribution to model+route. we can give access to a dashboard demo.
[07:54] Priya: for the pilot data residency
our data can't leave region eu-west-1. can you host in that region?
[08:01] Marco: yes, we have EU regions; for hosted we can pin region, for Private we'll deploy in your VPC. we'll confirm the region availability in the follow-up.
[08:12] Marta: one more on fallback policies
in case Dedicated nodes are full, can requests fallback to hosted cheaper models?
[08:19] Jonah: yes
smart routing allows policy-based fallback by latency or cost, with automatic rollbacks and A/B routing. we can pre-define model variants.
[08:30] Aisha: quick recap and next steps: we'll send pricing and Dedicated SKUs, Jonah shares security docs and benchmarks, Evan provides traffic profile and sample data for pilot, Priya confirms success criteria.
[08:44] Priya: i'll confirm success criteria by Friday.
[08:47] Evan: i'll pull traffic histograms and concurrent session estimates and drop them in the shared folder.
[08:52] Marta: sounds good. any blockers on our side? not that i see.
[08:57] Marco: just to note
if you want we can run a micro-benchmark this week with a subset of your traffic; it takes a day to configure.
[09:06] Aisha: great
we'll do that as an option. thanks everyone.
[09:10] (meeting ends)
